nav.apiHint: Keys, curl, smart home & AI agents

user.apiIntro: With personal API keys, scripts, your smart home or AI agents like Claude Code and Codex read and change your tasks, lists, notes and inbox: via curl or MCP, with the same permissions. Notes as well as reading and sorting the inbox work over MCP only.

mcp.title: Connect AI agents (MCP)
mcp.intro: MindSift is an MCP server: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor and your own agents use the same keys and permissions as curl, just in the form agents expect. claude.ai and ChatGPT connect without a key: MindSift asks what the agent may do while connecting.
mcp.connectorHint: In claude.ai, enter this address under Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector (in ChatGPT likewise as a connector or app). While connecting, MindSift opens: sign in, choose permissions, allow. The connection appears in the list above, where you can change or disconnect it; unused, it ends by itself after a while.
mcp.needsBaseUrl: Connecting via claude.ai and ChatGPT needs OAuth, which requires <c>BASE_URL</c> in the server configuration. Ask the person running MindSift to set it.
mcp.toolsHint: The agent only sees the tools the key or connection is allowed to use; access works as it does for you.

api.intro: A key connects Home Assistant, n8n, your own scripts or AI agents (Claude Code, Codex …) with MindSift. You set what it may do per area with Read, Create and Change (“Change” switches “Read” on too); this applies to curl and MCP alike, except that notes as well as reading and sorting the inbox are available over MCP only. Settings stay locked for keys. Whatever a key creates or changes in tasks and lists carries its name as a badge.
api.readExample: Reading, e.g. what is due today (permission “Read tasks”):
api.readFilters: Filters: <c>due=today</c>, <c>due=overdue</c> or a date (<c>YYYY-MM-DD</c>, due up to and including), <c>status=open|done</c>, <c>taskListId</c>. Lists: <c>GET /api/v1/lists</c> and <c>/lists/ID</c>. With “Change” also <c>PATCH /api/v1/thoughts/ID</c> (e.g. <c>{"isCompleted": true}</c>).

appearance.title: Appearance & single-file CSS themes
appearance.intro: Every theme is a single, self-contained CSS file that bundles all colors, surfaces, contrast and corner radii in 6 fixed groups.
appearance.linkPreviewsHint: A card with title, description and a small image above bullets with a web address. The MindSift server fetches the page for this, not your browser. Applies to this device; single previews can be hidden with ✕.
appearance.journalHint: One note per day, below each other with a calendar – at the top of the notes sidebar. Switching it off only hides it; the days stay as notes. Applies to this device.
appearance.cornersHint: Rounded or square – regardless of the theme. Applies to this device.
appearance.modeHint: “Like the system” switches within the color family with the device's light/dark mode.
appearance.bordersHint: Without borders, buttons are only slightly shaded. Applies to this device.
appearance.accentHint: Replaces the theme's accent color (buttons, links, highlights). Applies to this device.

custom.blocks: A theme is CSS with 6 blocks: 1. accent color, 2. surfaces, 3. text colors, 4. borders & shadows, 5. status colors and 6. corners. The easiest start is the template with your own values. Saved themes live on the server and are available on all your devices.
custom.copyFailed: Copying is not possible – use “Paste template” or the download.
custom.saveFailed: The theme could not be saved
custom.deleteFailed: The theme could not be deleted

doneTasks.title: Done tasks
doneTasks.text: Then move to the task trash.

retention.title: Retention
retention.intro: How long done and deleted things stay, counted from checking off or deleting. In shared task lists, lists and notes, the setting of the person who owns them applies.

voice.title: Voice input
voice.intro: What the microphone in MindSift uses to turn your speech into text.
voice.serverHint: The recording only goes to the speech recognition server of this MindSift installation. Works in every browser.
voice.browserHint: The browser's speech recognition. The text appears right while you speak; Chrome and Edge send the recording to Google or Microsoft for this. Firefox does not have it.
voice.languageIntro: The language you speak into the microphone, also ones the app is not available in.
voice.languageAutoHint: Whisper detects the language of each recording itself, handy if you speak German one time and Italian the next. A fixed language is recognized a little more reliably.
voice.languageAutoBrowser: The browser's speech recognition cannot detect the language and uses the app language. Automatic detection works with the Whisper server.

data.title: Export & import
data.intro: Download your data as a backup or Markdown archive, restore server backups or import MindSift data and Obsidian vaults.
data.backupHint: All your thoughts, tasks, notes and lists as JSON, with the images and voice notes of your notes, packed into a ZIP file. “Import MindSift data” restores it completely. The <c>Obsidian</c> folder holds everything as Markdown as well, which Obsidian or any text editor opens directly, even without MindSift.
data.importHint: An import creates everything anew and changes nothing that exists. Before importing you see what will be created.
data.vaultHint: All notes as <c>.md</c> files in your folder structure (with title, tags and date in the header), tasks per list under <c>Aufgaben/</c> in the format of the Obsidian Tasks plugin, lists under <c>Listen/</c>, images and voice notes under <c>attachments/</c>. Notes shared with you are included.
data.importMindSiftHint: Restore your own backup: backup (<c>.zip</c> or <c>.json</c>) or Markdown archive (<c>.zip</c>). Notes go back to their folders; task lists with subtasks, due dates and priorities as well as lists are restored.
data.importObsidianHint: Vault as <c>.zip</c>. All notes land in a folder of their own named after the vault; subfolders are kept. Checkboxes stay checkboxes in the note, frontmatter tags become #hashtags. Images and audio files a note embeds (<c>![[image.png]]</c> or <c>![](image.png)</c>) are imported; other attachments like PDFs are not.

private.text: Nobody shares with others: no sharing with people, no groups.

organizations.title: 2. Within organizations (recommended)

server.title: Server basics & sharing
server.intro: As server admin you decide who may share with whom, whether names are suggested while typing and whether notes can be shared by public link.
server.privateWebhooks: Allow alarm webhooks into the local network
server.privateWebhooksHint: Default: Discord and webhook alarms only go to public https addresses. When on, targets in the home network are allowed too (e.g. Home Assistant at 192.168.x.x or via Tailscale), there also over http. The server itself (localhost) and cloud metadata always stay blocked.

mode.approval: With approval – anyone may register, an admin approves
mode.domain: Only certain email domains – active right away
mode.domainApproval: Domains right away, everyone else after approval

server.verifyHint: New accounts without an invitation get a link by email and only become active afterwards (with approval they then reach you). Unconfirmed accounts are deleted after 48 hours.
server.switchWarning: Switching to “{{mode}}” removes {{count}} shares and group memberships that are no longer allowed afterwards.
server.registrationHint: Who may create an account on the sign-in screen. Invite links and codes always work. You approve waiting accounts under “Users & invitations”.
server.registrationFixed: Set by the environment (<c>REGISTRATION_MODE</c> / <c>REGISTRATION_DOMAINS</c>) and not changeable here.
server.verifyNeedsMail: Only takes effect with a configured mail server and <c>BASE_URL</c>.
server.retentionNeverHint: When on, everyone can choose “never” under Account settings → Retention and keep done and deleted things. When off, “never” falls back to the area's default (e.g. 30 days).
server.mcpHint: When on, Claude Code, Codex & co. can access MindSift with an API key, and claude.ai or ChatGPT as a connector. When off, the MCP endpoint and the connector sign-in are switched off; existing connector connections pause, API keys keep working via curl.
server.peopleSearchHint: On, matching names are suggested when sharing and in groups. Off, people need the exact e-mail address or username; those already working on something together still see each other’s names there.
server.publicLinksHint: Owners can share a note read only by link, also with people without an account, optionally with a password. Links always expire and stay out of search engines. Off, no existing link works any more.
server.linkPreviewsHint: When a bullet holds only a web address, the MindSift server fetches the page and shows its title, description and picture as a card. Off, the server fetches no pages, and the app shows neither preview cards nor the switch per device.
server.pushKnownOnly: Push only via known push services
server.pushKnownOnlyHint: Default: push notifications go to the push service the browser names (any https address). Switched on, only to the services of Google (Chrome, Edge, Android), Mozilla (Firefox), Apple (Safari) and Microsoft (Windows). Devices using other services then get no push messages.
server.mfaRequiredHint: Those affected who have no authenticator app and no passkey yet set one up right after their next sign-in and can do nothing else before. API keys and AI connections keep working.

oidc.title: Sign-in with OIDC
oidc.hint: Set up by the OIDC_* environment variables; shown here only.
oidc.notConfigured: Not set up. With OIDC_ISSUER, OIDC_CLIENT_ID and OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET everyone signs in with a provider such as Authentik, Authelia or Keycloak (see README).
oidc.offNoBaseUrl: Switched off: BASE_URL is missing. The provider needs the address it sends people back to.
oidc.unreachable: The provider does not answer right now: {{error}}

admin.title: Server administration
admin.subtitle: Users, invites, organizations, sharing & mail server
admin.demo: Disabled in the demo: server settings, email and accounts can only be viewed here.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.intro: A person can belong to several organizations. In the “Within organizations” mode people share only with those they have at least one in common with; every group belongs to one organization. Click an organization to add or remove members.
orgs.notActive: The current sharing mode is not “Within organizations”; memberships have no effect right now.
orgs.deleteWarning_one: The {{count}} member loses the shares, groups and assignments that were only allowed through this organization.
orgs.deleteWarning_other: The {{count}} members lose the shares, groups and assignments that were only allowed through this organization.
orgs.removeWarning_one: {{name}} leaves “{{org}}”. {{count}} share or group membership that was only allowed through this organization goes with it.
orgs.removeWarning_other: {{name}} leaves “{{org}}”. {{count}} shares and group memberships that were only allowed through this organization go with it.

smtp.title: Email / SMTP server for task alarms
smtp.intro: Configure the outgoing mail server with Docker Compose environment variables or right here in the interface (stored in the SQLite database).
smtp.tlsHint: Port 465: TLS from the start of the connection, otherwise STARTTLS. When on, nothing is sent without encryption.
smtp.skipVerifyHint: Only for internal mail servers with a self-signed certificate or a different name. The connection stays encrypted, but the server is no longer verified.
smtp.testHint: Sends a test email right away with the details entered above.
smtp.fromNameHint: Shown to the recipient as the sender. Empty = “MindSift”; a name right in the address (“Name <address>”) takes precedence.
smtp.passwordKept: Saved – leave empty for no change
smtp.passwordUnreadable: The stored password can no longer be decrypted: the server's key (SECRETS_KEY or secrets.key) has changed. No email goes out until you enter it again and save.
smtp.save: Save SMTP configuration to the database

import.mergeHint: Keep existing data, add the backup next to it.
import.restoreWarning: Caution: your current data in the chosen areas ({{sections}}) will be replaced by the backup and deleted for good once it has been imported completely (if that fails, they stay as they are). Content others shared with you is kept.

sessions.endFailed: The session could not be ended

backups.serverHint: Automatic daily backups of your data on the server (if the administration has switched them on).
backups.mergeHint: Keep what exists, add the backup next to it.
backups.autoHint: Daily a dump of the whole database and a backup per user under <c>backups/</c> in the data directory. This protects against mistakes, not against a broken disk: back up the folder somewhere else too.
backups.restoreHint: Restoring a database dump: stop the container, replace <c>mindsift.db</c> with the unpacked file (<c>gunzip</c>), start the container. Single users restore their own data in the account settings.
backups.restored: Restored: {{notes}} notes, {{tasks}} tasks, {{lists}} lists, {{inbox}} thoughts, {{themes}} themes.
backups.deletedHint: When an admin or user manager deletes an account, its backups stay here until the retention period ends. So someone deleted by mistake gets their data back: download a backup and import it in the new account under Account settings → Export & import. Accounts their owners delete lose their backups at once.

password.title: Change password
password.hint: At least 8 characters, a whole sentence is welcome: every character counts. All other devices are signed out afterwards.
password.saved: Password changed. All other devices were signed out.
password.failed: The password could not be changed
password.noMatch: The two new passwords do not match
password.setHint: You sign in with {{name}} and need no password of your own. With a password you can also sign in directly; MindSift asks {{name}} to confirm.
password.setHintAdmin: Signing in with a password is switched off; only administrators have emergency access at /?login=password in case {{name}} is down. Set the password for it here.

security.title: Security
security.intro: Your password, two-factor sign-in and the devices you are signed in on.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.intro: Besides the password, signing in asks for a second factor: a code from an authenticator app, such as Aegis, 2FAS, Google or Microsoft Authenticator or your password manager, or a passkey (see below).
twoFactor.offHint: Once it is on, a stolen password alone is no longer enough to sign in.
twoFactor.demo: Not available in the demo: all visitors share the accounts.
twoFactor.loadFailed: The state of two-factor sign-in could not be loaded
twoFactor.scanHint: Scan the code with your authenticator app. If that does not work, type in the key.
twoFactor.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app
twoFactor.codeHint: The app now shows a six-digit code. Enter it to switch two-factor sign-in on.
twoFactor.codesIntro: Without access to the app you sign in with one of these codes; each works once. Keep them safe, for example in your password manager or printed out. They are shown only now.
twoFactor.codesFileTitle: MindSift recovery codes for {{account}} (each works once)
twoFactor.codesLow: Make new ones before they run out.
twoFactor.newCodesHint: You get ten new codes, the previous ones stop working. To confirm: your password and a current code of the app (or a recovery code).
twoFactor.disableHint: Afterwards the password alone signs in again; recovery codes and trusted devices are deleted. To confirm: your password and a current code of the app (or a recovery code).
twoFactor.codeOrRecovery: Code of the app or recovery code
twoFactor.trustedHint_one: Marked as trusted when signing in: they ask for no code for {{count}} day. “End all sessions”, a new password and switching off end the trust.
twoFactor.trustedHint_other: Marked as trusted when signing in: they ask for no code for {{count}} days. “End all sessions”, a new password and switching off end the trust.
twoFactor.appOffWithPasskeys: You can set up an authenticator app in addition to your passkeys.
twoFactor.disableAppHint: The authenticator app is removed. Your passkeys stay, and so do recovery codes and trusted devices. To confirm: your password and a second factor.
twoFactor.appRemoved: Authenticator app removed. Two-factor sign-in stays on with your passkeys.
twoFactor.newCodesHintPasskey: You get ten new codes, the earlier ones stop working. To confirm: your password and a second factor: your passkey, a code of the app or a recovery code.
twoFactor.setupConfirmHint: Your account already has passkeys: also confirm with one of them or a recovery code.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: With a passkey you sign in by fingerprint, face recognition or device PIN: without a password, or after the password as a second factor. A passkey only works on this site and can neither be intercepted nor entered on a fake site.
passkeys.nameHint: So you recognize it later, e.g. “Phone” or “Laptop”. The browser asks for your fingerprint, face or PIN next.
passkeys.addedFirst: Passkey added. Two-factor sign-in is on now: after the password, signing in asks for the passkey.
passkeys.syncedHint: Kept in a password manager or account (e.g. iCloud, Google) and available on your other devices.
passkeys.removeHint: “{{name}}” no longer signs you in afterwards. Delete it in the password manager or the device settings too. To confirm: your password and a second factor.
passkeys.removeLast: This is your last second factor: two-factor sign-in is switched off, recovery codes and trusted devices are deleted. The password alone signs in again afterwards.
passkeys.removedOff: Passkey removed. Two-factor sign-in is off.
passkeys.unsupported: This browser cannot use passkeys. Use a current browser or another device.
passkeys.off_no_base_url: Passkeys are off on this server: they need a fixed address. The administrator has to set BASE_URL with https. The authenticator app works without it.
passkeys.off_not_https: Passkeys are off on this server: they only work over https. The administrator has to set BASE_URL to an https address. The authenticator app works without it.
passkeys.off_ip_address: Passkeys are off on this server: they need a host name instead of an IP address in BASE_URL. The authenticator app works without it.

confirm.title: Confirm with your second factor
confirm.intro: This change also needs your second factor.

oidc.title: Sign-in with {{name}}
oidc.linked: You sign in with {{name}}. You confirm sensitive changes such as a new address, a password, API keys or deleting by signing in to {{name}} again.
oidc.notLinked: Link your account to {{name}} to sign in there as well. You need your password to confirm.
oidc.confirmIntro: Sign in to {{name}} once more to confirm. You then come back here and can make the change within the next five minutes.
oidc.confirmFirst: Please confirm the change with {{name}} first.
oidc.confirmHint: You confirm by signing in to {{name}} again.
oidc.confirmedDone: Confirmed. You can make the change within the next five minutes.
oidc.linkedDone: Your account is now linked to {{name}}.
